parts.note: Dom is a title given to certain monks, especially Benedictines
taken as written
something empty holds nothing, and nothing is the letter O

explanation.surface: A monk standing in a cape with nothing in its pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monk' looks like the subject, but the definition is 'cape' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a loose hooded cloak worn at masquerades, a kind of cape.

clue.text: Go lightly through the tulips in song

definitions.text: Go lightly through the tulips in song

parts.words: Go lightly through the tulips in song
parts.note: the title of a famous old popular song describes stepping softly on the toes among flowers

explanation.surface: Walking delicately through a flowerbed, as a song says.
explanation.walkthrough: The song is 'Tiptoe Through the Tulips', a 1929 hit later revived by Tiny Tim.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk on the balls of the feet is to step softly and quietly, as in the old song title.

clue.text: Footballers quickly get to the point repeatedly before the finish

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the last one

parts.note: presto is the musical direction for a quick tempo
N is the abbreviation for north, a point of the compass
the compass point is given again, this time written out in full as north
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Footballers rushing to make their point again and again until the match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get to' is a link. The compass point appears twice: once as its abbreviation N, then 'repeatedly' gives it again in full. PRESTON NORTH END is an English football club from Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston North End is an English professional football club, so its players are footballers.

clue.text: Finger hesitantly used by one compiling alphabetical list

parts.note: the index finger is the forefinger, so finger gives index
er is the sound of someone speaking hesitantly

explanation.surface: A hesitant finger used by someone working down an alphabetical list.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who compiles a book's index, an alphabetical list of topics with page numbers.

clue.text: As new like a boiled sweet?

definitions.meaning: in perfect, unused condition, as an item for sale may be described
humorously, in the state of a mint, a peppermint candy

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means pristine and unused; read literally it describes being in the condition of a mint sweet.

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
a trail is a track or path

explanation.surface: Studying the track a vapour trail leaves in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The streak of condensed water vapour left behind by a high-flying aircraft.

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the phrase are put into disorder

explanation.surface: A cleaner being marked down on an inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of BE MARKED.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedmaker is a college servant who makes the beds and tidies rooms, especially at Cambridge.

clue.text: Right in place I leave the positive electron

indicators.note: in tells us one letter is set inside the other word
leave means the letter I goes out of the word for place

parts.note: a position is a place

explanation.surface: A physics instruction about putting things right and leaving a positive particle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' removes an I from POSITION, giving POSITON; 'in' then puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This antiparticle has the mass of an electron but carries a positive charge.

clue.text: Caught, no prescribed dose arranged to follow

indicators.note: to follow puts the second piece after the first

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of dose are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient caught out, having had no prescribed dose of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' gives OSED. 'prescribed' only dresses the surface, making the dose sound medical.
explanation.definitionFit: Noosed means caught in a loop of rope, as a snare or lasso traps an animal.

clue.text: No end of American money? It isn't clear

indicators.note: no end of means the final letter is taken off

parts.note: a dime is a ten-cent American coin

explanation.surface: Wondering whether there's no limit to American wealth, but it's unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'endless amounts of', but it removes the last letter E from DIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dim is faint or obscure, hard to see clearly.

indicators.note: infiltrating means one piece gets inside another
new signals that the letters of dates are formed afresh

parts.note: 1ST is the usual abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: Feeling disgust when a first date goes badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives DASTE from the anagram, and 'infiltrating' slips the abbreviation for first in just after its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a feeling of dislike or revulsion, much like disgust.

definitions.meaning: eventually, after some while has passed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means punctual, and also means eventually, as in 'it will heal given a while'.

clue.text: A fresh fall of snow will conceal the evidence

definitions.text: A fresh fall of snow will conceal the evidence

parts.words: A fresh fall of snow will conceal the evidence
parts.note: new snow hides footprints, which is literally what the idiom for hiding evidence of one's actions describes

explanation.surface: Snow falling over a crime scene and hiding the clues.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to hide the evidence of what you have done, literally to hide your footprints.

parts.note: Vi is the usual short form of the name Violet

explanation.surface: A woman called Violet travelling along an old Roman road.
explanation.definitionFit: Via is the Latin word for a road, as in the Via Appia.

definitions.meaning: locating something, as in following a lost item's path
a reproduction made by drawing over the original through thin paper

explanation.definitionFit: Tracing means finding (tracing a missing person) and a duplicate drawing made through translucent paper.

definitions.meaning: resistance or backlash against a change

explanation.definitionFit: A reaction can be resistance to change, and any reply prompted by something.

clue.text: Order nothing from unit of a special service brigade

definitions.text: unit of a special service brigade

parts.note: a command is an order
O stands for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: An order of nothing coming from a special forces unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Commando units are elite special forces formations trained for raids.

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: paltry means mean or meagre

explanation.surface: Nervous animals with a stingy sound to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' is a witty way to describe chickens and other fowl, which flap about but barely fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic fowl such as chickens and ducks are winged creatures, and notoriously skittish.

parts.note: the British phrase pairing a hot drink with sympathy offered to someone upset

explanation.surface: Something that goes along with sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'tea and sympathy' is the standard comfort offered to someone in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuppa is the traditional companion of sympathy in the British phrase 'tea and sympathy'.

clue.text: Spring not working in fortunate circumstances

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
a machine that is off is not working

explanation.surface: A spring that has stopped flowing in a lucky place.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well off means being wealthy or comfortably placed.

clue.text: Hit leading swindler, one found at sea

parts.note: to hammer is to hit
to head is to lead
a shark is a swindler or con man

explanation.surface: Striking the chief con man.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammerhead is a shark with a flattened, T-shaped head, living in the ocean.

parts.note: to hit is to strike
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: An order to hit a woman right here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hither is an old word meaning to this place, as in 'come hither'.

parts.note: re means about or concerning, which is one sense of of
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, the Italian Fascist dictator

explanation.surface: Telling a dictator to slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like a link but supplies RE, meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: To slim or diet is to lose weight.

indicators.note: without stopping means the word loses its final letter, its stop

parts.note: an ...é case is a briefcase

explanation.surface: Fastening a case shut without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without stopping' removes the last letter E from ATTACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach something is to fix or join it on.

clue.text: Lake viewpoint their leader leaves given leeway

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

indicators.note: leaves means a letter goes out of the word for viewpoint

parts.note: an attitude is a point of view

indicators.note: their leader is the opening letter of the word their

explanation.surface: Lakeside opinions shift once the leader departs, allowing some freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops one T (the leader of 'their') from the viewpoint word. 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is freedom of action or room to manoeuvre.

clue.text: I say oxygen is needed afterwards

indicators.note: afterwards puts the oxygen after the other piece

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means in 'take, say, a dog'
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A chemist insisting oxygen will be needed later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' looks like an exclamation, but 'I' is the definition and 'say' gives EG.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, one's sense of 'me'.

parts.note: to woo is to court
a den is a room

explanation.surface: An unbending courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court room' reads as a law court, but splits into court and room.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden means stiff and lacking flexibility, as in a wooden performance.

definitions.meaning: the given name of the famous Victorian nursing pioneer

explanation.definitionFit: The nursing pioneer Nightingale was named after the Tuscan city where she was born.
